x: Olly Flynn of Basildon managed to win in 52:01 mins. Len Duquemin was the second Bels man home, with Ray Middleton and John Moullin backing up.
A battle evolved between five competitors; Flynn, Lightman, Tolley, Court and Lawton. This group later split, with Flynn and Lightman breaking away to finish in that order.

Olly Flynn led from 5k to the finish while further back Carl Lawton was well placed in the first 20. Disqualification of Lightman, Thorpe and Wallwork enabled him to gain places without trying and eventually he ended up 10th.
First home was Brian Adams (Leicester) in 19:57.6 followed by Olly Flynn (Basildon), Peter Marlow (Southend) and Roger Mills (Ilford) so Carl was in very good company.

About a mile after the start the holder, Olly Flynn (Basildon), had opened up a small lead but everybody seemed to be going at a terrific rate (just over 7 minute miles for the leaders); Carl was in the leading group.

After five kilos Olly Flynn, Roger Mills and Brian Adams were away battling for Individual honours and they finished in that order. Then came the leading group which contained Carl and Graham, Ray soon appeared but where was our fourth man?
At 5KM Jobin led in 22:14 with Sawall 22:16 and then a gap until England's Olly Flynn passed the checkpoint with Erikson in 22:37 and Graham 22:54.
At the end of the first lap (covered in less than 17 minutes) Olly Flynn (Basildon) had opened up a gap on Brian Adams (Leicester) who was clear of the rest of the field.
To the race itself, the early leaders were Olly Flynn, Mike Parker, Brian Adams and Amos Seddon with Carl not too far back. The team race looked good for Ilford A.C. who had many well up.
